reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes OneCoin packages priced from €100 to €5,000, linking payment to token and coin allocations and commissions for referrals and network activity. It urges viewers to join and partner with the team while claiming substantial future account value and exceptional participant earnings. Although the chart labels its values as predictions and the income slide says earnings are not guaranteed, the pitch uses these financial claims as part of its recruitment solicitation.

opening.argument: Judge the forecasts as forecasts, not promises. The presentation shows projected coin prices alongside a disclaimer that the chart is based on predictions and depends on members' commitment and effort. It separately says income is not guaranteed and may vary with effort, commitment, and skill. The speaker also invites viewers to research the person behind the company. These qualifications do not prove the opportunity is sound, but they matter when deciding whether the video presents speculative returns as certain. Its strongest earnings figures should be read against the uncertainty the presentation itself discloses.

citations.quote: You could do all the research that you want on Google about this woman.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited package prices and referral bonuses establish what the presentation offers, not that its forecasts are guaranteed or its claims knowingly false. Even the account-value example turns on a stated condition: “If it goes to $2.” The income slide expressly cautions that earnings are not guaranteed. A paid, commission-bearing opportunity warrants scrutiny, but those features alone do not erase the stated uncertainty.

citations.quote: If it goes to $2, you're talking about 96,000 euros is what your account will be worth.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The disclaimers do not change the pitch's central transaction. Viewers are offered paid packages, and a purchase by someone in a participant's network is expressly linked to a bonus. The closing urges viewers to partner with the team now. That recruitment mechanism and call to act remain present even if future coin prices and individual income are uncertain.

opening.argument: Much of this presentation teaches the vocabulary and mechanics it asks viewers to evaluate. It explains cryptocurrency exchange by comparison with trading conventional currencies, describes lessons with interactive videos, manuals and quizzes, and walks through how tokens would convert into coins in a package example. That explanatory material gives a viewer more than an unexplained earnings claim: it sets out what the proposed packages contain and how the stated figures are calculated. The presence of a compensation-plan explanation does not, by itself, make every instructional portion a deceptive solicitation.

citations.quote: this is the cryptocurrency exchange where you could trade different currencies amongst each other
All educational packages would provide trading skills in the form of interactive videos, manuals, quizzes and lots more.
the 60,000 tokens are going to convert into 1 Coins at approximately 5 to 1

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening quotes accurately identify referral and network payments, but explanation of a compensation formula is not proof that the described payouts occurred or that the speaker concealed the formula. The package slide lays out prices and contents together, giving viewers a basis to assess the offer. The judge should distinguish describing a business model from independently establishing fraud within it.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The lessons are offered inside a sales presentation, not as a detached tutorial. The speaker tells viewers that recruiting a package buyer earns a commission and that network purchases can pay even when the buyer was not personally referred. The presentation ends by urging viewers to partner with the team. Explaining those mechanics makes the recruitment offer more concrete; it does not displace it.

that's somebody that you didn't even personally know or refer and they could be 100 levels down from you.
position yourself for success and partner with our team today

opening.argument: The offer is presented as a priced package with stated contents, including education, tokens and other benefits, rather than as an unexplained request for money. The package slide itemizes tiers and discloses an additional one-off registration fee. The speaker says there is no monthly commitment after purchase. Referral and network commissions are plainly described, so they should not be treated as a hidden term. On this record, the judge can identify a promotional offer and its compensation rules, but cannot verify that the represented assets lack value or that purchasers cannot receive the stated package contents.

citations.quote: there's no auto ships, there's no monthly commitment, once you buy your package that's it
if you refer somebody you're gonna get a commission You're also going to get paid from a network bonus

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's strongest evidence is the paid downline mechanism; the defense need not deny it. But the quoted network example states a proposed bonus for a package purchase, not evidence of an actual payment, a guaranteed return, or failure to deliver the listed contents. The same presentation says packages include education and that income is not guaranteed. Those limits matter before treating the offer itself as proof of deception.

citations.quote: they decide to buy a 5,000 euro package, the Tycoon package, you're gonna to earn a 500 dollar bonus
All educational packages would provide trading skills in the form of interactive videos, manuals, quizzes and lots more.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Itemizing products and fees does not make the compensation structure ordinary retail commerce. The presentation ties earnings to a recruit's paid package and to business volume on the weaker side of a network; it also describes matching bonuses across four generations. Those are affirmative features of the promoted opportunity, not gaps that depend on proving whether any particular purchaser received a payout.
